item.text: {"question_id":"6B.2","answer":"The record shows implemented access mechanisms, especially social protection: Takaful and Karama provided conditional transfers for poor households with children and unconditional transfers for poor older people, orphans, widows, and persons with disabilities; by December 2023 it reportedly reached 4.67 million households, with a dynamic registry linking beneficiaries to health insurance and food subsidies and substantial outreach administration (BATCH-0020-E012; BATCH-0020-E013; BATCH-0020-E014). Universal Health Insurance had enrolled over five million people in six Phase 1 governorates and contracted more than 322 providers, but the figures are cumulative and not specifically year-end 2023, and they do not establish affordability, quality, uptake, or outcomes (BATCH-0023-E003). Emergency food-security support helped maintain uninterrupted bread subsidies from December 2022 through February 2023, but this was World Bank-financed and jointly implemented, limiting attribution to el-Sisi personally (BATCH-0023-E002). Egypt also established organized medical evacuation and treatment arrangements for patients from Gaza in November 2023, but these were external humanitarian operations rather than evidence of broad domestic service access (BATCH-0018-E004; BATCH-0019-E007). Access remained substantially incomplete and unequal: nearly 30 percent of Egyptians lived in poverty; fewer than one quarter of children were enrolled in public pre-primary education; at least one million school-age children with disabilities and many refugee and migrant children were out of school; and internet access varied by region, gender, wealth, and education (BATCH-0005-E006; BATCH-0005-E007; BATCH-0009-R02-E006). Transfers covered only about one-third of families living in or near poverty and were eroded by inflation and currency devaluation, while electricity cutbacks disrupted work, health care, and water access, particularly in rural and impoverished areas (BATCH-0009-R07-E010; BATCH-0009-R07-E011). Affordability and effective administration were further weakened by austerity, reduced health and education spending, higher service prices, and low-quality or fee-based higher-education provision (BATCH-0008-E004; BATCH-0015-E008; BATCH-0008-E022). Housing access was weak: historical social-housing delivery fell far below its target and access for precarious or poor households was described as largely theoretical; water and sanitation investment and allocation were also criticized for favoring affluent new cities, while monitoring and feasibility assessment were insufficient (BATCH-0009-R10-E010; BATCH-0009-R10-E013; BATCH-0009-R10-E014). Thus, the supplied evidence supports real but uneven program delivery and some access expansion, not broad, demonstrably affordable, effective, and equitable access across the full service portfolio in 2023.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0020-E013","BATCH-0020-E014","BATCH-0023-E003","BATCH-0023-E002","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0019-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0005-E007","BATCH-0009-R02-E006","BATCH-0009-R07-E010","BATCH-0009-R07-E011","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0015-E008","BATCH-0008-E022","BATCH-0009-R10-E010","BATCH-0009-R10-E013","BATCH-0009-R10-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most evidence does not isolate el-Sisi’s personal decisions from collective government, donor, World Bank, WHO, or subnational implementation.","Several favorable indicators are cumulative, retrospective, planned, or outside the target-year calendar and do not establish 2023 year-end access, affordability, quality, uptake, or outcomes.","Evidence remains fragmented for water, sanitation, housing, food security, and education, with limited comparable measurement of exclusion, service quality, and territorial variation.","The supplied record does not provide executed-budget evidence sufficient to establish that spending translated into broad effective access.","The housing and water evidence includes historical or continuing conditions rather than a complete 2023 assessment."],"corrections_made":["Removed World Bank-supported food-security operations and Gaza medical arrangements as evidence of broad domestic service access; retained them only with explicit scope and attribution limits.","Recast Universal Health Insurance enrollment and provider figures as cumulative, non-year-end indicators that do not prove affordability, quality, uptake, or outcomes.","Added contrary evidence on housing access, water allocation, monitoring, and feasibility assessment.","Removed the unsupported characterization of UNICEF-described programs as demonstrated service expansion; UNICEF evidence is used for government program aims and persistent access gaps.","Qualified the transfer coverage and poverty evidence according to the supplied source wording and period."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review would be warranted if year-specific executed budgets, enrollment and utilization data, service-quality measures, or household-survey evidence become available.","Further review could clarify attribution between el-Sisi, ministries, local governments, international financiers, and implementing partners.","The current evidence does not consistently distinguish access from affordability, uptake, effective quality, or durable outcomes across all listed domains."]}
